title: TCG Grading Services (2026)
verdict: TCG grading services in 2026 start at $10 a card at CGC and $15 at AGS, and AGS is our pick because the price includes eight subgrades, a report and no value cap.

CGC is the value pick among the large graders at $10 a card in bulk, and a PSA 10 still brings the most on chase cards. TAG gives a strong defect report on modern cards but does not take Yu-Gi-Oh!. Ace Grading is the local choice in the UK.

sections.h: What to check on TCG cards before you submit
list: Holo scratches. Tilt the card under a lamp and look across the foil.
Whitening on back edges and corners.
Print lines and roller marks from the factory.
Centering on the back as well as the front.
Dents and binder dings, which often show only at an angle.

why: Human grading is a judgment made in seconds, and it varies. AGS replaces the judgment with a measurement: a 3D laser maps the card, software scores centering, corners, edges and surface, and the grade follows from the numbers. That is why AGS says a regrade rarely moves.
Most cards qualify. AGS grades TCG and sports, old and new, signed, miscut and error cards, and does not turn away damaged cards unless they are illegible. It does not take jumbo sizes.
Turnaround is counted in days. AGS quotes 20 business days or less from the day your cards are confirmed, with 10 and 5 business day bulk tiers at $20 and $30 a card.

faq.q: Which are the main TCG grading services?
faq.a: AGS for a measured grade on TCG cards at $15 to $18. CGC for the lowest price from a large grader. PSA when a chase card's resale price is the priority.

faq.q: Which cards does TAG not accept?
faq.a: TAG's site says it does not currently accept Yu-Gi-Oh!, pre-1989 cards, memorabilia cards or cards thicker than 50pt.

faq.q: Do AGS slabs hold resale value?
faq.a: AGS slabs sell, and the report gives buyers something to check. PSA holders still bring the highest prices on most cards. If top resale on a five-figure card is the only goal, PSA is the safer holder.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.

faq.q: Are miscut and error cards graded?
faq.a: At AGS, yes. Miscut and error cards are measured and graded, and damaged cards are not rejected unless they are illegible.
